source_audit: The EE vblank host path publishes before pacing. Legacy pacing waits only while software audio exceeds about 80ms.
The present packet traverses EE -> VU -> renderer. Publication can block in ring insertion or the two-outstanding-present guard; post_wait is not pure GPU time.
Slow Fuji buckets have increased publication wait and mostly negligible intentional pacing wait. Near-60 Thunderhead/Onuris spend more time in pacing but retain adverse callback tails.
The separate v19 CPU/RIP profile supports residual VU continuation and GS preparation investigation, not attribution of each human-session spike to a single helper.

Next bounded diagnosis should separate the two publication wait sites and producer/renderer CPU work in an automated diagnostic, preserving queue depth/order and keeping probes separate from pure FPS. No further unchanged-binary manual log round is requested.
limits: These are descriptive unpaired sessions with different lengths, driving, effects, focus and uncontrolled external host load, not a causal speedup comparison.
One checkpoint per environment does not certify all tracks/classes/Mirror or independently prove six complete races, victory, results or progression-save/readback.
The lowest Skorost bucket (20-25s,36.25FPS) has a stationary scene clock and cannot be assigned to active driving; it remains visible.
Scene time is not player race/result time or proof of original timing. Even near-60 simulation means do not certify original cadence.
Callbacks precede GS presentation; they are not scanout or physical audio/input latency. Software queue values are not hardware underrun proof.
Normal exits and unchanged cards establish preservation, not a successful new race-result save.
Separate sessions do not constitute a continuous30min test. No human test of the rejected v20 candidate or new gameplay release is claimed.
